transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’ve just been forgetting things more than I’m comfortable with. Little things I usually keep track of—returning calls, getting a registration form turned in, remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask for help.
When did you first start noticing these memory lapses, and how long has this been going on?

I think it got noticeably harder when I started my evening certificate program… about 15 months ago. It may have been there before, but that’s when it started feeling like more than just normal forgetfulness.
Besides the forgetfulness, have you noticed feeling more down, anxious, or worried than usual over these past 15 months?
Not really… I mean, I get stressed when I realize I forgot something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been more down or anxious overall. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
Have these memory issues affected your ability to manage daily responsibilities—like paying bills, managing medications, or performing your job duties—on your own?

I’m still managing on my own, mostly. Bills and things like that haven’t fallen apart. But… at work I’ve missed some small follow-ups, and with school I’ve missed a few deadlines. Not huge things, but enough that I’m worried people will notice, especially since I’d like to move into an Office Manager role eventually.
Besides forgetting things, have you noticed any other changes—like trouble finding the right words, getting confused about directions, or difficulty planning and organizing tasks?

Mostly organizing, I guess. I can usually keep up at work, but since starting the evening classes, things kind of pile up—my desk, my class folder, email reminders. Then I waste time just trying to figure out what I’m supposed to do first.
Since these memory and organization problems started about 15 months ago, would you say they’ve been getting steadily worse over time, or have they stayed about the same?
I wouldn’t say it’s been steadily getting worse. It’s more that since I started the evening certificate program, about 15 months ago, it’s just been harder to keep on top of things.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions—like thyroid problems, sleep apnea, vitamin deficiencies, or a past head injury—that your doctor has mentioned could affect your memory or thinking?
Not that I know of. No doctor’s mentioned anything like that to me.
Since starting the evening program 15 months ago, has your sleep schedule or the amount of sleep you get each night changed?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think it changed a lot, but with classes some nights I probably get to bed later. I haven’t really kept track.
Before starting this evening program 15 months ago, did you ever struggle with similar issues of forgetfulness, disorganization, or trouble focusing—say, back in school or earlier in your career?
Yeah… I guess so. Even when I was little, I’d forget things like permission slips, or lose homework in my backpack. My mom or the teacher usually had to remind me step by step to get projects done.
Growing up, did teachers or family members ever comment that your forgetfulness or trouble staying organized was a recurring problem both at home and at school, not just occasionally?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, in elementary school it came up a lot. I’d forget permission slips, lose homework in my backpack, and my mom or teacher would have to kind of walk me through projects step by step.
